props.note: Game reconstruction: an enlarged cluster standing in for Hiolo North's iron-oxide-draped, low-temperature venting (~1,300 m, ~20-40 degC fluids). The existing smoker-cluster feature supplies the silhouette and plume; its roughly 9 m tallest stack exceeds the earlier 5 m art cap and is not a surveyed Hiolo structure or evidence of black-smoker sulfides. Layout and size are invented. The basalt material hint retains the iron-stained palette.
Second, smaller mound at Hiolo North, same rationale as hiolo-north-chimney-1.

Game reconstruction: a vent cluster at Hiolo South (~1,274 m, ~47 degC mean fluid temperature -- the warmest of the Hiolo sites), near the 'cauliflower' iron-mat orifice described in the source literature. The existing smoker-cluster feature supplies an invented layout and size for the diffuse iron-oxide vent site, not a surveyed sulfide edifice.

Game addition: pillow-lava heap with iron-oxide staining and orange iron-bacteria mats east-southeast of the Hiolo North chimneys, leaving the vent mounds visible on approach; the seamount is basaltic and its summit vents host Fe-oxidising mats (Emerson & Moyer 2002). Exact layout and size are invented.
